title: Audit log relay resilience, backoff strategies, and SIEM compatibility
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Enterprise customers using Redwood Private and Dedicated are receiving intermittent duplicate or out-of-order audit events in downstream SIEMs (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, generic webhook sinks). Root causes observed: transient network errors, receiver-side throttling or 429s, retry storms from naive exponential backoff, and lack of strong deduplication keys across tenants. Goal: Build a hardened relay design and operational contract that ensures at-least-once delivery with bounded duplication, strong ordering guarantees for per-session events where required, and clear integration recipes for common SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog, SumoLogic) and generic webhook endpoints.
proposal_summary: Introduce a Relay Layer between audit-event producers and external sinks that provides per-tenant delivery queues, idempotency tokens, ordered sequence windows, pluggable backoff policies, and a tenant-scoped Dead Letter Queue. Provide integration adapters for Splunk HEC and Datadog HTTP intake with standardized signing (HMAC) and TLS options. Expose per-sink SLAs, retry/exponential backoff presets, and observable metrics for success rate, duplicate rate, and delivery latency.
design_decisions: Per-tenant persistent queues: durable write-ahead log (WAL) per tenant to survive process restarts and allow replay
Idempotency via (tenant_id, event_id) composite key with event TTL and configurable dedup window (default 7 days)
Ordering modes: 'none' (best-effort), 'per-stream' (session/connection ordered) and 'strict' (global per-tenant ordering) with tradeoffs on throughput and latency
Backoff: use jittered capped exponential backoff with receiver-aware guidance (use Retry-After if provided). Default max attempts = 10; for 429/503 prefer aggressive backoff with longer cap
DLQ: tenant-scoped DLQ that retains failure metadata and raw payload for investigations; automatic alert on DLQ spike relative to baseline
Batching: dynamic batching by destination type (Splunk HEC supports events batch; generic webhooks do not) with max batch size and time window configuration
Security: TLS 1.2+/mTLS option for private deployments, request signing HMAC-SHA256 for webhook authenticity, and schema version headers for evolution
Observability: emit token-level metrics (per-tenant), delivery attempts histogram, duplicate ratio, average ack latency, and SLO breach counters
tradeoffs: Strict ordering reduces throughput and increases tail latency because it serializes delivery per-tenant stream
Longer dedup windows increase storage for seen-ids database; TTL default tuned to 7 days to balance forensic requirements vs storage costs
Aggressive retry improves delivery probability but may exacerbate downstream overload; receiver-aware backoff reduces this risk when endpoints provide Retry-After
DLQ retention increases storage and exposes PII risk; require tenant-level redaction and admin controls for DLQ access
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end audit event flow to Splunk HEC with >99.95% success under normal load (no downstream faults)
During a simulated receiver 429 storm, relay respects Retry-After and reduces retry rate by >= 80% compared to baseline
Deduplication reduces observed delivery duplicates to <0.1% for a synthetic test workload with deliberate retransmits
DLQ events are searchable in Console and include full failure reason, last attempt timestamp, and raw payload
Documentation updated with Splunk/Datadog webhook recipes and integration checklist
implementation_tasks: Spec: finalise relay API surface and per-sink adapter contract (ENG design doc link)
Storage: implement tenant WAL and seen-ids KV store with TTL support
Adapters: build Splunk HEC adapter with batching and HEC token handling
Adapters: build Datadog HTTP adapter with rate-limit handling and DD API keys
Delivery: implement backoff manager that honors Retry-After and receiver hints
DLQ: implement tenant-scoped DLQ UI endpoints and export tooling
Tests: integration test harness to simulate noisy downstreams and verify SLOs
Docs: runbook and integration guides for customers and SEs
